description: What to do about each refusal and unsupported code: the usual cause and the action, for docs/reference/refusal-codes.md and docs/guides/troubleshooting.md. The codes, meanings, requirements and detection stages come from spec/refusal-codes.json. go/internal/tools/docgen fails when a code there has no entry here, or the reverse.

no_manifest.cause: The path is not a dataset root, or the producer has not committed the dataset yet: the manifest is the last file written (COMMIT-1).
no_manifest.action: Check the path points at the directory or prefix that holds manifest.json. If a producer is still writing, wait for its commit.

invalid_manifest.cause: A hand-written or hand-edited manifest: a missing or misspelled member, unpadded or URL-safe base64 in a key bound, a part path outside the root, part bounds out of order or overlapping.
invalid_manifest.action: Check the manifest against spec/manifest.schema.json, then the rules of §3. The error's detail names the member.

unsupported_version.cause: The dataset was written for a different draft revision or format version than this reader supports.
unsupported_version.action: Use a reader release that supports the dataset's version pair, or rewrite the dataset with a producer of this reader's version.

missing_part.cause: A part was deleted or never published, or the manifest names a path that differs from the file (case, directory).
missing_part.action: Restore the part, or rewrite the dataset. A producer must make every part durable before it commits the manifest (COMMIT-1).

part_mismatch.cause: A part was replaced or rewritten after the manifest was committed, or the producer recorded the size or row count before the file was finished.
part_mismatch.action: Treat the dataset as damaged and rewrite it. Parts are immutable once committed (COMMIT-2); a producer records each part's size and rows from the sealed file.

invalid_footer.cause: A truncated or partially copied part, a file that is not Parquet, or a writer that puts column chunks in other files (file_path).
invalid_footer.action: Compare the part's size and checksum with the source. Copy parts whole and only after they are complete.

stamp_mismatch.cause: The part lacks the five seekparquet.* footer stamps or disagrees with the manifest. pyarrow drops them when called with store_schema=False.
stamp_mismatch.action: Write the stamps into the part's footer key-value metadata (STAMP-1), exactly as the manifest states the version, schema id and key. See the producing guide.

invalid_key_column.cause: The key column is nullable, not BYTE_ARRAY, carries an annotation other than STRING, or lacks TYPE_ORDER. DuckDB's COPY TO writes the key OPTIONAL.
invalid_key_column.action: Declare the key a non-nullable binary or string column (Parquet REQUIRED BYTE_ARRAY) with column_orders set (KEY-1, KEY-5).

inconsistent_column.cause: Parts written with different schemas: a column changed type, nullability or nesting between parts.
inconsistent_column.action: Write every part with one schema. A part may omit a column (COL-2), but a column it has must match the other parts.

missing_sorting_columns.cause: The writer was not told the rows are sorted, so it wrote no sorting_columns, or wrote the key descending or not first.
missing_sorting_columns.action: Declare the key as the first sorting column, ascending, on every row group (RG-1). In pyarrow: sorting_columns=[pq.SortingColumn(i)].

missing_page_index.cause: The writer did not write a page index. pyarrow writes none unless called with write_page_index=True; some writers drop the ColumnIndex for very long keys.
missing_page_index.action: Enable the page index for the key column (RG-2). In pyarrow: write_page_index=True.

invalid_page_index.cause: A writer that shortens page bounds incorrectly (for example keys beginning with 0xFF bytes), or a page index edited or damaged after writing.
invalid_page_index.action: Rewrite the part with a writer whose bounds hold every key of the page (RG-5). Validate at the profile level to find every such page.

invalid_key.cause: An empty key, or bytes that are not UTF-8 in a key column annotated STRING.
invalid_key.action: Drop or encode empty keys before writing (KEY-2). Store keys that are not UTF-8 in an unannotated binary key column (KEY-6).

key_order.cause: Rows sorted as signed bytes, by a string collation or locale, or by UTF-16 code units; or duplicate keys in a dataset whose manifest declares keys unique.
key_order.action: Sort keys by unsigned byte order (KEY-3), and declare key.unique false when keys repeat.

invalid_parquet.cause: A damaged page: bit rot, a bad copy, or a writer bug in compression or encoding.
invalid_parquet.action: Rewrite or restore the part. Validate at the full level to find every damaged page; reads report only the pages they decode.

bounds_mismatch.cause: The manifest's min_key or max_key was taken from intended bounds or from shortened page-index bounds, not from the part's actual first and last keys.
bounds_mismatch.action: Write the manifest's bounds from the first and last keys actually written to each part (PART-3).

digest_mismatch.cause: A part changed after its digest was recorded, or the digest was computed over different bytes.
digest_mismatch.action: Treat the part as damaged and restore or rewrite it. Compute the digest over the sealed file's bytes.

unsupported_encoding.cause: A codec or encoding outside what this reader decodes, such as BROTLI in the Java reader.
unsupported_encoding.action: Rewrite the dataset with a baseline codec: UNCOMPRESSED, SNAPPY, GZIP, ZSTD or LZ4_RAW (ENC-1). Requests that do not touch the column still succeed.

unsupported_projection.cause: The request projects a nested or repeated column.
unsupported_projection.action: Project only top-level, non-repeated columns (COL-3), or read the part with a general Parquet reader.

unsupported_encryption.cause: The part uses Parquet modular encryption.
unsupported_encryption.action: Read the part with a Parquet reader that decrypts, or write the dataset unencrypted (FILE-2).
